lines.text: Sea glass takes decades to frost.
It starts as pieces of old bottles and tableware.
Waves and sand tumble the broken pieces until the edges turn smooth.
Real frosted sea glass is covered in tiny curved pits.
Green and brown are among the most common colors.
Red and orange are among the rarest.
Sunlight can turn old clear glass made with manganese purple.

For a ring, a thin silver rim called a bezel holds it.

post.caption: Sea glass takes decades to frost. It starts as pieces of old bottles and tableware. Waves and sand tumble the broken pieces until the edges turn smooth. Real frosted sea glass is covered in tiny curved pits. Green and brown are among the most common colors. Red and orange are among the rarest. Sunlight can turn old clear glass made with manganese purple. Each July, a sea glass festival in Connecticut gathers collectors and jewelers. A contest there has a category for frosted bottles. Jewelers drill a small hole with a diamond bit for a pendant. For a ring, a thin silver rim called a bezel holds it.
